questions.text: In a doubly linked list the number of pointers affected for an insertion operation will be
questions.solution:
The number of pointers changed depends on where the node is inserted: in the middle, 4 links change (2 in the new node and one in each neighbour); at the head or tail, fewer.

Answer: Depends on the nodes of doubly linked list

questions.text: If the post order traversal gives ab -cd * + then the label of the nodes 1,2,3.. will be
questions.solution:
Postorder ab[latex]-[/latex]cd*+ means the root is +, its left subtree is a[latex]-[/latex]b and its right subtree is c*d. So node 1 = +, node 2 = [latex]-[/latex], node 3 = *, and leaves 4, 5, 6, 7 = a, b, c, d.

Answer: +, -, *, a, b, c, d

questions.text: Which of the following data structure is useful in traversing a given graph by breadth first search?
questions.solution:
BFS visits nodes level by level, first in first out, so it uses a queue. (DFS uses a stack.)

Answer: Queue

questions.text:
Given two statements
Insertion of an element should be done at the last node of the circular list
Deletion of an element should be done at the last node of the circular list
questions.solution:
In a circular list there is no rule that insertion or deletion must happen at the last node; elements can be inserted or deleted at any position. Both statements are false.

Answer: Both are false

questions.text:
The pre-order transversal of a binary search tree is given by 12, 8, 6, 2, 7, 9, 10, 16, 15, 19,
17, 20. Then the post-order traversal of this tree is:
questions.solution:
Build the BST from the preorder: root 12; left subtree 8 (left 6 with children 2, 7; right 9 with right child 10); right subtree 16 (left 15; right 19 with children 17, 20).

Postorder: 2, 7, 6, 10, 9, 8, 15, 17, 20, 19, 16, 12

Answer: 2,7,6,10,9,8,15,17,20,19,16,12
